beat: Missile fields, silos, and their afterlives — Atlas D/E/F, Titan I/II, Nike Ajax/Hercules, Minuteman, Safeguard. First discovery sweep. US-only. Emphasis on the divergence between EXIST (near-trivially documented for this class) and STAT/CTRL/FUNC (the live propositions once a site leaves federal hands).
method_notes:
RETRIEVAL STATE, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT GOVERNS EVERYTHING BELOW. WebFetch is non-functional in this environment. I attempted it four times against four different classes of host — a state agency (cdphe.colorado.gov), a veterans' association site (556sms.com), Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org) and an enthusiast register (themilitarystandard.com) — and every one returned EGRESS_BLOCKED. That is not a .gov/.mil-specific block; it is total. I therefore opened ZERO documents. Every source below is recorded from a WebSearch result block: a title, a URL, and a summary produced by the search tool. In BES terms every observation I could offer is receipt_state = UNRESOLVED-UNREACHABLE, receipt_class = R-NONE, membership = V0, arithmetically inert. V is empty for every proposition on every candidate.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE GRADES. Two rules interact. CAP-5 (V = empty) caps everything at F. But §9.4 step 2 returns X when SCI < 0.5 and the provisional grade would be D/E/F/R — and my search completeness against the canonical set for this beat is close to zero: I could not reach the NARA catalog, DTIC, GSA disposal records, FUDS, county recorders, NRHP/NPGallery, USGS HTMC, MILCON J-books, or any state environmental repository. So the correct BES answer for essentially every proposition here is X — NOT ASSESSED, specifically §10.5's 'X — VERIFICATION PENDING'. I have written X as the proposed_band throughout and appended, as an explicitly labelled analyst projection, the band I expect the proposition to reach once the named receipts resolve. The projection is my judgement and is not a grade.

I want to be blunt about one thing: when a search snippet summarises the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment's Titan I page, I have evidence that a CDPHE page about Titan I complexes exists and that a summarising model read something on it. I do not have evidence of what the page says. The distinction is recorded per source in what_it_actually_shows and I have tried not to let it slip anywhere.

WHY THIS BEAT IS DIFFERENT FROM THE REST OF THE REGISTER — the finding I most want carried forward. For Atlas, Titan, Nike, Minuteman and Safeguard, §6.1's 'absence of a record is not evidence of absence' largely INVERTS. These were unclassified-existence programs, congressionally appropriated, built by the Corps of Engineers, disposed of through GSA, recorded in county deed books, and in many cases surveyed to HAER/NRHP standard. The expected-record profile is dense and public: county deed X3, GSA disposal X2, MILCON line 1950-90 unclassified X3, USGS HTMC quad X3, FUDS listing X2, USACE construction records X1 (RG 77 archive gap). For this class, a missing deed IS surprising. The register should not extend to a decommissioned Atlas F the epistemic charity it correctly extends to Greenbrier-in-1991. Conversely: the class-level record is so good that instance-level EXIST/LOCT/CTRL should be cheap to push to A once egress works, and the register's effort should go almost entirely to STAT and current CTRL, exactly as GRADING.md §4.3's SILO/LAUNCH-FACILITY catalog says.

WHAT WORKED. Backward tracing worked even without fetch. Three of the four hollow claims below were caught by noticing that a numeric detail travels intact through a dozen unrelated outlets while an independent technical source gives a different number — the distinctive-error test of §5.1.7 operating on shared FACTS rather than shared wording, which is what makes it survive paraphrase and machine regeneration. The 'epoxy-resin concrete, walls almost ten feet thick' formulation is the clearest specimen I found on this beat.

WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH. (1) Not one coordinate. Where I give one it is a number I saw inside a search snippet, flagged claimed-only, never derived. (2) Not one site designation confirmed against an Air Force list — I have deliberately left several as 'designation unconfirmed' rather than guess, because a wrong site number is exactly the confabulation this register exists to catch and Atlas/Titan designations (556-5, 579-1, 724-C, Complex 2B/2C) are format-regular and therefore cheap to hallucinate. (3) No parcel, deed, or GSA disposal record for any candidate. (4) No verification that any 'currently operating' claim is currently true — several rest solely on a press release or an operator's own website.

AGENT INDEPENDENCE. Nothing in this file corroborates anything else in this file. If another agent on another beat returns the same claim, that is the same indexed web surfaced twice, not two witnesses (§5.0).

candidates.name: Stanley R. Mickelsen Safeguard Complex — Missile Site Radar building ("the Nekoma pyramid")
candidates.era: Constructed c. 1970–1975; declared operational October 1975; deactivated February–April 1976; surplused and sold 2012; resold 2020; under a data-centre redevelopment agreement from 2022

location.description: Near Nekoma, Cavalier County, North Dakota. Town-level only.
location.basis: Town name appears consistently across every search snippet. I have no coordinate from any source I saw and did not derive one. No parcel identifier retrieved.

candidates.claim_origin: The facility's existence was never concealed — it was a treaty-limited ABM site built under public appropriation and reported contemporaneously. The claim lineage that matters here is not EXIST but the modern ownership-and-function story, and it is traceable to specific dated acts: (a) a 2012 GSA-adjacent surplus sale to the Spring Creek Hutterite Colony of Forbes ND for $530,000, reported in ND regional press and repeated everywhere since; (b) a 2020 resale of portions including the pyramid to the Cavalier County Job Development Authority for $462,900; (c) a 26 July 2022 announcement from the office of Gov. Doug Burgum that Bitzero Blockchain Inc. had signed a binding agreement to acquire the pyramid and invest ~$500M converting it to a data centre. Every 'Nekoma is now a crypto HQ' item I found descends from (c). The $530,000 and $462,900 figures propagate as fixed constants across outlets, which is a single-lineage signature, not corroboration.
candidates.lineage_note: Three genuinely distinct origins are visible: the historical/military record (many independent institutional roots), the county property transactions (would be independent if the recorder's index were reachable — two bureaucracies recording the same event for unrelated purposes, §5.1.7's access test), and the 2022 corporate announcement (ONE origin, the governor's press office relaying a company's statement, replicated into dozens of trade and listicle outlets). Bleeding Heartland's Feb 2024 and Nov 2024 reporting is the only item I found that is plausibly independent of (c), because it reports on the ABSENCE of the thing (c) predicted — it could have been written without (c) existing only in the trivial sense that it is about (c). I count it as a distinct lineage for the UNDERCUTS direction.
candidates.mundane_alternative: For EXIST/HRDN there is no mundane alternative worth naming — this is A01/A12 territory and both fail immediately; the structure is a photographed landmark. The live nulls are on the modern propositions. For FUNC(operating data centre): A07, 'an announced but substantially unbuilt commercial data-centre project, with a small pilot deployment used to keep an incentive package and a purchase option alive.' What would distinguish it: an interconnection agreement or a filed load study with the serving cooperative showing contracted MW at the site; a county building permit with a valuation; property-tax assessment change reflecting installed equipment; an FCC/state utility filing; PeeringDB or IP-transit route announcements originating at the site. What will NOT distinguish it: the company's own press release, the governor's press release, a photograph of the exterior, or the number '$500 million'. For CTRL(Bitzero): A09/A11-adjacent — 'a signed agreement that has not closed, or has closed only in part' — distinguished by the Cavalier County recorder's deed index and nothing else.
candidates.expected_records: For a 1970s Army ABM complex the expected-record set is dense and mostly public: MILCON appropriations lines and Senate/House hearing testimony (X3 — Safeguard was one of the most publicly debated construction programs of its decade); Corps of Engineers construction records in RG 77 (X1, archive-gap flag, ~96% undigitised); ABM Treaty and SALT compliance documentation (X3); GSA/Army surplus disposal records for the 2012 sale (X2); Cavalier County recorder deed index for 2012, 2020 and any 2022+ conveyance (X3 — the universal floor, and its absence WOULD be surprising); USGS HTMC quadrangle depiction (X3); environmental records for a site with 1970s-era fuels and solvents (X2). Their absence would be surprising in every case. This is the opposite of a COG-facility silence profile, and the register should say so on the entry page.
candidates.confidence_note: EXIST is about as close to unarguable as anything on this beat and would go to A in one afternoon of working receipts. Everything about the last four years is genuinely uncertain and rests on announcements. I have deliberately graded the 2025 'operating with 2.5MW available' claim harshly because its only source is the company's own newswire release, which is textbook §2.5 self-attestation: the author is the claimant and the probative content is the claim.

candidates.name: Safeguard Remote Sprint Launch Site 3 (RSL-3), Cavalier County, North Dakota
candidates.era: Built c. 1970–1974 as one of four RSL sites supporting the Mickelsen complex; deactivated 1976; GSA auction 2013; privately owned and publicly toured since

location.description: Cavalier County, North Dakota, one of four dispersed RSL sites around the Mickelsen complex.
location.basis: County-level from search snippets only. No coordinate retrieved. Atlas Obscura and a tour operator's own site both exist for this location and either would give a coordinate if fetchable.

candidates.claim_origin: The disposal story traces to a documented 2013 GSA auction of the four RSL sites. Specific figures propagate: RSL-1 at 41 acres for $64,111; RSL-2 at 36 acres to named buyers Anna and Jim Cleveland for $85,000; RSL-3 to Mel Sann in 2013. Those precise, odd numbers ($64,111) are exactly the kind of detail that indicates a single documentary origin — most likely the GSA auction results themselves, relayed through one or two ND press items and then replicated. I could not identify the first publication. Treat the four-site figure set as ONE lineage until the GSA record resolves.
candidates.lineage_note: Everything I saw about RSL ownership is consistent with a single origin in the GSA sale record plus one regional feature article (the oscarzero.wordpress.com 'Blazing Skies' post reads like the compiler). The tour operator's own site (rsl3.com) is self-published and its probative content about ownership IS the claim — but a person conducting paid public tours of a property they claim to own is making a checkable assertion against the county recorder, which is what makes this candidate worth working rather than dismissing.
candidates.mundane_alternative: For EXIST: A01 fails outright — there are photographs and a ticketed tour. The interesting null is on HRDN/EXTN: A05, 'a hardened-looking but shallow launcher and equipment vault, whose depth and blast rating are described from memory and marketing rather than from drawings.' Distinguished by: the Safeguard RSL as-built drawings (Corps of Engineers / Army Safeguard System Command), or the GSA disposal description, which for surplus federal property routinely recites structures and dimensions because a buyer needs them. That GSA description is the cheapest high-value document on this candidate.
candidates.expected_records: GSA surplus real-property disposal record for the 2013 auction, including the sale notice and the conveyance (X2 — and for an auctioned site the notice is normally public, so absence would be mildly surprising); Cavalier County recorder deed, 2013 and any subsequent transfer (X3, universal floor); MILCON/appropriations under the Safeguard program (X3 at program level, X1 at individual-RSL level); Corps of Engineers construction records RG 77 (X1, archive-gap); environmental/asbestos survey preceding disposal (X2 — federal disposals normally carry one); USGS HTMC depiction (X3).
candidates.confidence_note: This is the kind of entry I think the register most needs: entirely real, entirely boring, extensively surveyed at class level, and with a live private-ownership question that a single county-recorder query would settle. It is the B-04 shape (ordinary and well-attested at class level, thin at instance level) but with a tour operator making instance-level assertions that are checkable.

candidates.mundane_alternative: For EXIST there is a real and interesting null here, which is rare: A01 — 'no substantial enclosed structure remains; the launch duct was collapsed and backfilled and what survives is a filled void and surface pads, not a structure.' Aerial imagery showing pads does not distinguish them.

What would distinguish it: the Army site list's launch/control site split for BA-79; the state property record's description; HAER documentation, since many Nike sites were HAER-recorded with measured drawings deposited at the Library of Congress; or a photograph of an elevator in a magazine. candidates.claim_origin: Institutional throughout. The State Historical Society of North Dakota operates the site and publishes its history; SAH Archipedia (Society of Architectural Historians) carries a scholarly architectural entry keyed ND-01-GG3. The claim I most want to pin is the START-related one: that the November-33 launch facility was NOT destroyed in the general silo demolition but was preserved — filled with gravel, blast door closed and welded or fixed in the closed position — under an arrangement permitting museum retention. candidates.claim_origin: Entirely institutional and, unusually, bilateral. The destruction is a treaty-verified fact: START I required elimination by controlled explosive demolition, and the resulting excavation had to remain open for ninety days so that the other party's national technical means could confirm it. Arms Control Today reported the first of 150 Minuteman III silo destructions in 1999 and the last on 24 August 2001. refuted_or_hollow.claim: Atlas F missile silos have walls almost ten feet thick, made from 'super-hardened, bomb-proof, epoxy-resin concrete', with rebar over three inches thick — making converted silos effectively nuclear-blast-proof homes.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: I could not identify the first publication, and I am saying that plainly rather than naming a culprit. What I CAN establish from my sweep: the formulation appears, in near-identical wording, across the silo-real-estate and silo-tourism corpus — a Kansas state tourism blog (travelks.com), a travel blog (getlostintheusa.com), a UK property listicle (loveproperty.com), an Adirondack regional feature, and the missilebases.com/20th Century Castles brokerage material. The wording travels as a unit: 'almost 10 feet thick', 'epoxy resin', 'rebar over three inches'. The most probable origin, on the structure of the corpus and on dating, is 1990s marketing copy from the 20th Century Castles brokerage — the entity that both created this market and wrote its first descriptions — but I did not run the dated negative receipt (Wayback CDX over missilebases.com and the pre-2000 corpus) that an ORIGIN grade requires, so that remains a hypothesis and I have not graded it.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: It contradicts an independent technical source in the same sweep. The Federation of American Scientists' Atlas silo description gives the surrounding reinforced-concrete wall as ABOUT 2.5 FEET THICK, and separately notes concrete on the SURFACE at nine feet. The tourism/brokerage version appears to have taken the surface-slab figure and reassigned it to the walls — a transposition, not an invention, which is why it survives casual checking and why it propagates so cleanly. 'Epoxy-resin concrete' is the tell: it is a distinctive, technical-sounding, hard-to-verify detail of exactly the kind that §5.1.7's distinctive-error test identifies as near-dispositive evidence of derivation, because regenerated and paraphrased text loses wording but keeps facts INCLUDING WRONG ONES. The register should treat the presence of 'epoxy resin' in any silo description as a lineage marker rather than as information. Note also the separate 100 psi overpressure figure circulating for Atlas F: that is a plausible design figure for the ORIGINAL structure and is a completely different claim from 'this converted home is blast-proof today'. Fifty years, a sale, and a residential fit-out sit between them.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: Real hardened Cold War structures, accurately described in one respect (thick concrete somewhere) and inaccurately in another (where), by parties with a commercial interest in the impressive reading, repeated by outlets with no capacity or incentive to check. No fabrication is required at any step. This is the ordinary way a wrong number becomes universal.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: The Nekoma pyramid (Stanley R. Mickelsen Safeguard Complex MSR) 'is now a crypto HQ' / is an operating $500 million data centre.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Traceable to a single dated act: the 26 July 2022 announcement from the office of Governor Doug Burgum that Bitzero Blockchain Inc. had signed a binding agreement with the Cavalier County Job Development Authority to acquire the pyramid, with a stated ~$500M expected investment and 35–50 jobs. Within 48 hours the same figures appear across KFYR, Valley News Live, KNOX, Grand Forks Herald, The Center Square, CSi, Walsh County Record, EIN Presswire and DataCenterDynamics. The consumer terminus is the loveproperty/lovemoney gallery headline asserting present-tense operation, syndicated onward through Yahoo. One origin, several dozen copies.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Not fabricated — hollow in the specific sense that the evidence is an ANNOUNCEMENT being reported as an ACCOMPLISHMENT. Against it: Bleeding Heartland raised management and ownership questions in February 2024, and reporting in my sweep indicates that as of November 2024, more than two years on, there was very little evidence of progress at the site and that state funds promised for it had not been used. The only source asserting present operation is a June 2025 PR Newswire release issued by the company itself, which under §2.5 is self-attesting — the author is the claimant and the probative content is the claim — and which describes 2.5MW available at a site announced for 300MW, a two-orders-of-magnitude gap that the headline framing does not survive. Nothing in the citation graph is an interconnection agreement, a permit, an assessment change, or a deed. Under CAP-2b, a FUNCTION claim with no verified instance-scope CLAIM-PROPERTY observation cannot exceed E, and that is the correct disposition. NOTE HONESTLY: this is not a refutation. It is a demonstration that the claim as circulated has no support of the kind that would settle it, and it may yet become true.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A02/A07-adjacent: an economic-development announcement with a state political sponsor, a purchase option or staged agreement, and a small pilot deployment sufficient to keep the arrangement alive — reported by a press ecosystem that treats announcements as events. DataCenterDynamics separately reports that at least two earlier attempts to turn Atlas silos in New Mexico into secure data centres or records storage never got off the ground, which is the base rate this claim should have been read against from the start.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: Some Colorado Titan I complexes have been 'adapted for alternate use like data storage'.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: A single unattributed clause in one enthusiast page (openroadcolorado.com, 'Titan 1 Missile Silos in Colorado'). I found no second source, no named operator, no company, no site, and no date. My targeted follow-up search for a Colorado Titan I data centre returned nothing but the same page, unrelated Titan-named companies, and a stock SEC filing for a firm called Titan Trading Analytics.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: It names nothing checkable. A data centre is one of the most externally visible commercial activities that can occupy a building — it needs contracted megawatts, an interconnection, a network presence, customers and usually a marketing website. The expected-record profile for an operating commercial data centre is X2–X3 across utility interconnection, county permits, assessed value and IP-transit route announcements, and NONE of it is present. Under §6.1 this is one of the cases where silence IS informative: absence of evidence for a covert federal facility carries nearly no information, but absence of evidence for a commercial data centre carries a great deal, because a commercial data centre has every incentive to be findable. This is the register's own asymmetry rule doing useful work in the direction people forget it runs.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: Almost certainly a garbled recollection of the well-documented general phenomenon of underground facilities being used for records storage and data centres — Iron Mountain at Boyers, the Kansas City limestone complexes — attached loosely to Colorado Titan I sites, which are in fact largely flooded, hazardous and under state environmental oversight for solvent contamination. The competing description in the SAME sweep — a 2024 county rescue operation inside a silo headlined 'Death around every corner' — is hard to reconcile with an operating data centre and is much better sourced.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: Decommissioned Atlas/Titan/Nike sites are entrances or nodes in a national network of deep underground military bases, connected by tunnels.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: The DUMB corpus, whose modern American form traces to a small self-published 1990s origin set — the Sauder/Schneider '129 deep underground military bases' material, which the calibration suite carries at F-03. In my own sweep the query surfaced deepundergroundmilitarybases.com and a silo.tips PDF host of 'Secret Underground Bases', which is the same corpus recirculating. Nothing in it originates on this beat; the missile-silo attachment is an accretion onto a claim structure that predates it.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Missile fields are the single worst possible substrate for this claim, and that is the interesting part. This is the most extensively surveyed, most thoroughly declassified, most completely disposed-of category of hardened American infrastructure that exists: Air Force site lists, GSA auction records, county deeds for every parcel, FUDS property records, state environmental files, NRHP nominations, HAER measured drawings, squadron veterans' associations publishing site-by-site histories, and — for the Minuteman population — a bilateral treaty verification regime under which an ADVERSARY GOVERNMENT was invited to confirm by satellite that each launcher had been destroyed and the hole left open for ninety days. The expected-record profile for a tunnel network connecting these sites would be X3 on spoil-volume accounting, X3 on construction procurement, X3 on county land records for the intervening right-of-way, and X3 on the treaty inventories. That silence is loudly informative. But §8.4 forbids R on negatives alone, and this claim earns F — SILENCE-DOMINATED, with V empty via §2.5, exactly as F-03 does. I want to be precise about the direction: the register is not saying 'no tunnels because we found nothing'. It is saying the claim has no verified support of any kind, and separately that the records which would exist do not.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A12/A11: real, individually documented, individually disposed-of military facilities of a known typology, aggregated into an imagined system by a corpus that predates and is indifferent to their actual records. The tunnels that genuinely exist — the cableways and utility tunnels between a Titan I silo and its control dome, the tunnel junctions of a Titan II complex — are real, documented, short, and connect a site to itself.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: Individual former Minuteman launch facilities in the Grand Forks field survive as intact hardened structures available for purchase and conversion.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: A conflation of two true things: (a) GSA did auction former 321st Missile Wing parcels to private buyers, with reported bids from about $6,000 to $17,800, reported by the Grand Forks Herald; and (b) former missile properties generally are bought and converted, which is true of Atlas and Titan sites and of Minuteman MISSILE ALERT FACILITIES. The conflation runs through the general silo-real-estate corpus rather than through any single identifiable source.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: The Minuteman LAUNCH FACILITIES in this population were destroyed before disposal, by treaty requirement — controlled explosive demolition with roughly 800 lb of explosives, the excavation left open for ninety days for verification. What was auctioned is in most cases the parcel and its surface remnants, not a usable subsurface structure. The two classes of property — a launch control facility with its intact underground capsule, and a launch facility with a demolished and backfilled duct — are routinely spoken of together as 'missile sites for sale' and are physically nothing alike. Recorded here because it is a live consumer-facing error rather than a fringe one: someone can lose money on it. The discriminating documents are the START elimination notifications and the GSA disposal descriptions, both enumerable.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: Two accurate facts about the same real estate market, describing two different asset classes, merged by imprecise category language. No one had to be wrong on purpose.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: The Adirondack Atlas F silo at Lewis, New York (556-5) houses a cosmic-ray / low-background detection facility for SUNY Plattsburgh researchers.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: One Adirondack Explorer feature ('Disco, Stout and Cosmic Rays'), whose headline itself implies three separate silo afterlives across the twelve-site Plattsburgh ring. In the summary I received, the cosmic-ray use was attributed to 'Site 5 in Lewis' in one sentence while the article's broader subject includes the Au Sable Forks site 556-6.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Recorded as UNRESOLVED rather than refuted, and I want the distinction preserved. The underlying activity is entirely plausible — a deep rock-cut void with low ambient background is genuinely attractive for low-background counting, and the physics literature contains many such shallow-underground facilities. What is missing is any second source: no publication, no technical report, no institutional record, no equipment-siting document names an Adirondack missile silo as a counting location. My targeted search returned only Gran Sasso, Felsenkeller, Dortmund and Argonne. Until a paper or an institutional record names the site, this is a magazine sentence, its site attribution is ambiguous between two silos twelve miles apart, and it should not be attached to either entry as a FEATURE. Flagged as a lead worth two minutes of a literature search once egress works.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A06 — an underground space used for ordinary purposes, to which a research use is loosely or retrospectively attached; or a real but small and undocumented university project; or a correct fact attached to the wrong one of twelve nearly identical sites. All three are ordinary and none require anyone to have said anything false.

coverage_gaps:
WHAT I DID NOT COVER, ranked by how much it costs the register.

1. THE ENTIRE CANONICAL SOURCE SET. Not one index was enumerated. No NARA catalog API walk of RG 77 / RG 341 / RG 342 by ancestorNaId; no DTIC search by originating lab report series (AFWL-TR, AFSWC-TR, DASA, DNA-TR, WES) which SOURCE-REGISTRY identifies as the richest corpus for hardened-structure engineering and which would settle nearly every HARDEN proposition in this file; no FUDS FeatureServer sweep filtered on Nike/Titan/Atlas/Minuteman property names, which is described as the best single geospatial source for decommissioned hardened infrastructure and which alone would produce hundreds of instance candidates with durable FUDS property-number join keys; no GSA disposal records; no county recorder queries anywhere; no NPGallery full-text search of NRHP nominations for 'blast door', 'hardened', 'shock isolation'; no USGS HTMC temporal stacks; no FCC ASR; no Chronicling America or state newspaper programs (Colorado Historic Newspapers, Wyoming, Nevada, New Mexico and Utah matter disproportionately here); no AAFM newsletter run or 'Taps for Missileers'; no Wayback CDX. Every one of these was blocked or unreachable. This is not a research plan I chose; it is the entire methodology of the register, unavailable.

2. WHOLE PROGRAMS ABSENT. Titan I in Washington (568th SMS, Larson AFB — I surfaced but did not develop a complex at Royal City/Quincy reported as flooded and used for technical diving, which is a genuinely unusual afterlife worth an entry); Titan I in Idaho, California and South Dakota; the Atlas E rings at Forbes, Fairchild and Lincoln beyond the single Kansas conversion; the entire Nike population outside two Maryland sites — roughly 250 defended-area sites nationally, with Ed Thelen's register as the ready-made enumeration and an acute succession risk attached to it (he died in 2024; SOURCE-REGISTRY says mirror it now, and I endorse that as urgent); Safeguard's Missile Site Radar remote launch sites RSL-1, RSL-2 and RSL-4; the Nike Zeus and Sprint/Spartan test infrastructure at Kwajalein and White Sands; Minuteman at Whiteman, Ellsworth and Malmstrom; Peacekeeper/MX basing including the Deep Basing and Closely Spaced Basing studies, which are a PROGRAM-class opportunity of the DUCC shape — heavily documented, never built, and currently unrepresented.

3. NIKE W-25, DAVIDSONVILLE, MARYLAND — deliberately left as a partial. It is now the Anne Arundel County Police Training Academy, it has a Maryland Department of the Environment Voluntary Cleanup Program document (a state regulator describing a former launch and control site for its own purposes), and it has a named scholarly monograph (Merle T. Cole's 'W-25: The Davidsonville Site and Maryland Air Defense, 1950–1974'). That combination — regulator plus scholar plus county reuse — is a stronger evidentiary structure than several candidates I did develop, and it should be first in the next cycle.

4. THE CONVERSION-FAILURE POPULATION. DataCenterDynamics reports at least two failed attempts to make New Mexico Atlas silos into secure data centres or records storage. Failed conversions are systematically absent from the corpus because nobody writes about a thing that did not happen, and they are exactly what the register should collect: they establish the base rate against which every announced conversion — Nekoma included — must be read. There is no index of them. Building one is a genuine contribution and would have to be done by working GSA disposal records and county deeds forward, not by searching.

5. NO SIGNED NEGATIVES. I produced no receipted negative searches. Every absence in this file is UNSEARCHED, not NEGATIVE, and per §6.2 an unsearched record class produces NO ROW — not a zero. Nothing here may be scored against any candidate as an absence.

6. THE ONE THING I MOST WANT THE NEXT CYCLE TO INHERIT. For this beat the register's default epistemic posture should be INVERTED relative to the COG beats. These programs were publicly appropriated, publicly built, publicly disposed of and in the Minuteman case adversarially verified. Missing records here are surprising, and the expected-record tables should carry a silo/launch-facility profile that says so explicitly, rather than defaulting to the classified-facility charity that is correct for Greenbrier-in-1991 and wrong for an Atlas F in Cloud County.
